title: The Anxious Generation
author: Jonathan Haidt
blurb: Around 2012, rates of anxiety, depression, and self-harm among teenagers began rising sharply across many wealthy countries. Social psychologist Jonathan Haidt argues the main cause was a Great Rewiring of childhood. In just a few years, kids moved from a play-based childhood, full of unsupervised time with friends, to a phone-based childhood spent on smartphones and social media. At the same time, fearful parenting cut back on the free play and independence children need to grow resilient. Haidt describes how this shift deprives kids of sleep, face-to-face connection, and focus, and how it fuels addiction. He explains why girls and boys tend to be harmed in different ways. Finally, he proposes four simple norms that families and schools can adopt together, because no single parent can solve this collective problem alone.

lessons.b: In the early 2010s, teen mental health declined sharply just as childhood moved from playgrounds to smartphones and social media.
